sessions.title: Keynote: Craft Beer vs. The World
sessions.description: Over a decade and a half on the beverage alcohol beat, Dave Infante has reported on how craft beer went from a "movement," to a "boom," to the rapidly maturing industry it is today. In his keynote presentation, he'll examine some of the biggest challenges facing today's craft brewer, dispel some popular mainstream-media myths, and highlight how the full-flavored beer segment still has opportunities to deliver on its promises of quality, innovation, and community. With incisive analysis, good data, and bad memes, Dave will examine the state of the industry from his unique vantage point, offering fresh ideas and perspective to Minnesota's craft brewers finding their way through the industry's so-called "second shakeout."

sessions.title: Brewing Bonds: Cultivating Community Partnerships to Increase Foot Traffic
sessions.description: As the craft beer industry continues to evolve, breweries are recognizing the significance of partnerships within their communities. This presentation will explore how engaging with local organizations can create impactful experiences that foster inclusivity and strengthen community ties while offering enjoyable options for visitors of many ages. Selected by the MNCBG DEI Committee.

sessions.title: Hop Quality Analysis for Dummies
sessions.description: Hops are one of your most important ingredients. Besides rubbing and sniffing, what can you do to analyze hop quality? In this presentation, we will cover physical hop pellet analysis, define Descriptive Hop Analysis, and introduce and define Comparative Aroma Analysis. You will leave with new skills to evaluate hops, tools that you can use to secure better quality hops, and most importantly a new mindset to better identify hops that meet your brewing goals. Selected by the MBAA.

sessions.title: Overdose Prevention Training (Narcan Training)
sessions.description: In this training participants will learn about the opioid epidemic and why this is something that is important for all of us to be aware of. The training will cover how to recognize an overdose, what naloxone/Narcan is and how it works, and how to administer it to save a life. Upon completion of this training, all attendees will be able to receive a free IM naloxone kit, certificate of completion, and continuing education credits for select licenses. Session will include free injectable naloxone kits and drug test strips to take back to the brewery. Narcan (nasal spray naloxone) kits can be purchased for an at-cost fee.Selected by the MNCBG DEI Committee.

sessions.title: State of the Hemp Market
sessions.description: What is the latest information on the MN and federal hemp market, and how should businesses approach this market while it is in flux? A great session for businesses looking for more clarity on the market's current state and how to plan going forward.

sessions.title: Winning in Distribution
sessions.description: Most breweries face challenges when it comes to succeeding in distribution. From understanding how the numbers impact the business as a whole to managing distributor relationships, running a sales team, and coordinating logistics, distribution is no easy feat. In this rigged game, wins can happen, though they often feel fleeting. Some breweries distribute out of necessity, while others seek the validation of seeing their beer on store shelves. Whatever your motivation, there are a few essential concepts you must embrace to find success in distribution. In this session, we’ll share these key concepts along with benchmarks to help you unlock the path to distribution success. Selected by the MNCBG Board.

sessions.title: Future Planning in Headwinds- Let's Get Creative
sessions.description: This panel discussion is all about embracing a positive and progressive mindset as we future plan for our businesses. Craft beer is facing headwinds, and the current regulatory structure in the state of Minnesota is quite restrictive, making mergers, acquisitions, or expansion through additional direct to retail impossible or impractical. So what do we do next?

sessions.title: Restaurant Hospitality for Breweries - Turning your Brewery into a Successful F&B Operation
sessions.description: Great beer gets people in the door. Thoughtful hospitality and a smart food concept keep them coming back. This session takes a practical, real-world look at how thoughtfully designed food and hospitality operations can elevate your brewery’s guest experience and long-term profitability. Food and beverage experts Sara Phelps and Michaelann Gillis will share insights into how breweries can successfully introduce, manage, or refine a food offering that fits their brand, space, and operational reality—without overcomplicating the taproom experience. We’ll dive into the details that matter most: building confident service teams, creating consistent guest experiences and designing taproom “steps of service” that run smoothly. Whether you’re looking to strengthen your current hospitality approach or considering adding a food and beverage component to your taproom, this conversation will help you see new opportunities to take your guest experience to the next level.

sessions.title: Stave New World: Methodologies for Managing the Modern (British) Brewer's Wood Cellar
sessions.description: Revolution Brewing Barrel Program Manager and Proprietor of Barrelponix, Marty Scott, pulls back the curtain on just what's happening to beer as it ages in (or on) wood. Through the concept of "Trinity", brewers and beverage makers will shed common misconceptions and learn methods for program optimization from both liquid and commercial perspectives. Learn how to infuse custom oak extractions into fresh beer anaerobically, or turn your existing barrel program up to eleven while maximizing the impact on your bottom line.

sessions.title: Telling Your Brand Story Online: How to Connect and Stand Out Online
sessions.description: In today’s crowded market, great beer isn’t enough—you need a story that connects. This session explores how breweries can use storytelling to build brand loyalty, deepen community ties, and stand out online without feeling salesy or overproduced. Attendees will learn a simple framework for turning everyday moments into meaningful content and walk away with actionable strategies to humanize their brand voice across platforms. Whether you’re a small taproom or a regional player, this talk will show you how to craft content that feels as intentional as the beer you brew.

sessions.title: The Guild’s Role in Today’s Industry: A Discussion on What You Need Now
sessions.description: The craft brewing industry has changed dramatically in the past few years, and your Guild needs to, too. Join leaders of the MN Craft Brewers Guild to provide feedback on the big-picture future of how your Craft Brewers Guild should best serve you - the members - in this challenging time. This is a discussion and listening session to help shape the Guild's future. All feedback - positive and critical - is welcome!

sessions.title: From Brewer to Boss: Equipping First-Time Leaders in the Brewery
sessions.description: Great breweries don’t fail because of bad beer; they struggle because great individual contributors are promoted into leadership without proper development. From Brewer to Boss is an interactive, workshop-style session designed to help brewery owners and managers equip first-time leaders with the tools they need to succeed. Participants will gain practical insights into why leadership requires training, how to reduce burnout in new managers, and how to build leaders who elevate both people and performance. Attendees will leave with immediately usable frameworks tailored specifically to brewery life.

sessions.title: Where Do We Go From Here When Here Keeps Changing?
sessions.description: The Legislative Committee of the MNCBG is a self nominating committee whose purpose is to “provide feedback and direction on behalf of the greater membership to the Guild’s Board of Directors”. The Committee is comprised of a Chair, Vice Chair, Communications officer and up to 7 other members. Current Committee Members are Mike Corneille, Jeremy Mathison, Jim Diley, Tessa Leung, Jon Erickson, and Bob Countryman.

sessions.title: Low & Non-Alcoholic "Off-Flavor" Sensory Workshop
sessions.description: Crafting quality low- and no-alcohol beers can be challenging. It can also be risky if not approached with a thorough understanding of the entire process, from raw ingredient selection all the way to stabilization in the package.This sensory workshop helps brewers identify some of the most common compounds behind the "worty" and vegetal off-flavors in NA beers, while also  exploring the science driving the complexities of their production.

sessions.title: S.A.L.E.S. Training: Selling Alcohol Legally, Effectively & Safely
sessions.description:
This workshop focuses on how hospitality, guest experience, and ethical sales drive success. By aligning everyday decisions, from legal compliance to team collaboration- you’ll learn to manage the customer experience to minimize risk and maximize revenue. This session equips your team to serve both safely and profitably.

Training by Robert Foster & the Minnesota Licensed Beverage Association. Robert Foster has worked in the hospitality industry since 1998, holding roles from busser to general manager. With experience spanning fine dining to multi-location operations, he’s led teams, created beverage programs, taught culinary classes, and consulted across the industry. For over 15 years, he has partnered with the MLBA, training countless businesses—from local restaurants to regional venues—on responsible alcohol sales and service. Now, Robert focuses on sales training, hospitality leadership, and empowering teams to serve legally, ethically, and confidently.

sessions.title: Your Taproom Is Already a Third Place — Act Like It
sessions.description: Third places have declined, but breweries have increasingly become a civic gathering space in many communities. This session explores how taprooms are already generating social capital and how we can plan, adapt, respond, and matter.

presenters.name: Alesha Ivey
presenters.bio: Alesha is the Technical Sales Manager for Lallemand Brewing here in Minnesota. After spending the last 10 years on the production side of the industry in both wine and beer, she loves having this new platform to help other brewers create quality focused and innovative products.

presenters.name: Audrey Robinson
presenters.bio: Little Thistle is a community-oriented brewery in Rochester MN. I like many small business employees wear a lot of hats and do my best not to drop one. As a team we work hard to create a welcoming atmosphere paired with delicious beer.

presenters.name: Ben Hugus
presenters.bio: Ben Hugus is the founder and CEO of Ursa Minor Brewing, a brand defined by bold craftsmanship and a commitment to continuous internal growth since its inception in 2018. Ursa Minor has experienced a remarkable trajectory- from 800 to nearly 5,000bbls in 7 years. Ben remains dedicated to scaling the brewery's impact while maintaining the passionate quality that defines the North Shore staple.

presenters.name: Ben Neitge
presenters.bio: Ben Neitge is the Events Coordinator at Forgotten Star Brewing, where he produces and manages hundreds of public and private events each year, from neighborhood gatherings to large-scale festivals. With a background in Sociology and Urban Studies from Augsburg University and over a decade in the Minneapolis music scene, he brings a community-centered, people-first approach to creating welcoming, revenue-driving experiences for breweries. Outside of work, he’s works as a fly fishing guide and is a proud father figure to two adopted kitty boys.
presenters.presentationTitle: Your Taproom Is Already a Third Place — Act Like It

presenters.name: Bob Galligan
presenters.bio: Bob Galligan began his brewing career hand canning in Austin Texas in 2012. Since then, he has been a brewer, tap room manager, salesperson, and quality and innovation manager. Most recently, he was the Sensory Specialist at Surly Brewing from 2017-2022. He served on the MNCBG Board in 2021 and joined in his current role as the Guild's Director of Government & Industry Relations in early 2022.
presenters.presentationTitle: The Guild’s Role in Today’s Industry: A Discussion on What You Need Now

presenters.name: Chris Farmand
presenters.bio: Chris often hears the question “Why do you care so much?” In 2010 Chris was fortunate enough to assist a craft brewery with their bookkeeping, compliance and taxes. This gave him a glimpse into the complexity of running a craft brewery. Shortly thereafter, he founded Small Batch Standard, which has become the premier financial agency for craft. Everyday, Chris and the SBS team are seeking the opportunity to assist the craft alcohol industry to generate more profit. Small Batch Standard helps breweries uncover profit through outsourced accounting, tax compliance, and benchmark consulting. Chris has worked with over 300 breweries and is driven by building long-lasting deep relationships. His answer, “Because I think you can win!” Chris graduated from the University of Florida with a Bachelor of Science in Business Finance in 2002. Then in 2006, he received his Master of Business Administration from the University of North Florida."

presenters.name: Dave Infante
presenters.bio: Dave is an award-winning journalist who covers the food and drink industries. He publishes Fingers, an independent newsletter about drinking in America. He also works as a contributing editor and columnist at VinePair, where he publishes the weekly beer-industry column Hop Take. He lives in Richmond, Virginia.
presenters.presentationTitle: Keynote: Craft Beer vs. The World

presenters.name: Dawn Finnie
presenters.bio: Dawn Finnie is the co-founder of Little Thistle Brewing Company in Rochester, MN. She’s had a love of craft beer in Minnesota for over 30 years and respects thoughtful brewing, community-driven taprooms, and beers with a good story. She has served on the Board of Directors and as board president of the MN Craft Brewers Guild.

presenters.name: Elliot Ginsburg
presenters.bio: Elliot has been representing alcohol beverage companies for over ten years on everything from trademark matters, to employee issues, to internal business disputes, to start-up financing and documentation, to regulatory issues, etc. He has built long-lasting relationships with his brewery clients, and has also guided many of them through various hemp/cannabis related issues. He has been working with cannabis businesses for over seven years.

presenters.name: Eric Sannerud
presenters.bio: Eric cares a lot about hops. As President of Sannerud Hop Consulting, Eric serves brewers, hop farmers, and hop marketers across North America with strategic marketing, product development, and education services. Eric serves Oregon hop farming families with West Coast Hop Breeding and provides expert hop market analysis and education in a free monthly newsletter called Hop Notes.

presenters.name: Jen Reise
presenters.bio: Jen Randolph Reise is one of Minnesota's leading cannabis business consultants, specializing in helping first-time entrepreneurs navigate the state's complex regulatory landscape. As founder of North Star Cannabis Consulting, Jen has guided over 500 entrepreneurs through business formation, regulatory compliance, and growth strategies. Her unique combination of legal training, entrepreneurial experience, and community-building expertise makes complex cannabis regulations accessible for business owners at every stage.

presenters.name: Jess Talley
presenters.bio: Jess is a association nonprofit specialist with 15 years in nonprofit administration. She joined the industry in 2018 as the Guild's first Marketing and Communications Manager, and was promoted to Executive Director in late 2021. She is responsible for the administration, budgeting, and management of the organization's services, programs, events, and staff, and works closely with the Board to ensure the Guild is carrying out our strategic goals and commitments to members.
presenters.presentationTitle: The Guild’s Role in Today’s Industry: A Discussion on What You Need Now

presenters.name: Jim Diley
presenters.bio: Jim Diley is the Co-Founder and COO of Fulton Brewing Company, and over the past 15 years has watched it grow from producing 94 BBLs in it's first year, to becoming a regional craft brewery. Jim currently serves on the MNCBG Board of Directors. Prior to starting Fulton, Jim worked in alcoholic beverages as an attorney helping others realize their goals.
presenters.presentationTitle: Where Do We Go From Here When Here Keeps Changing?

presenters.name: Jon Halper
presenters.bio: Jon Halper is the CEO and Owner of Top Ten Liquors, a Minnesota-based retail chain known for its curated selection, strong value, and exceptional customer service. Under his leadership, the company has become one of the state’s leading retailers of hemp-derived THC beverages and edibles, helping introduce thousands of consumers to the category through education, assortment, and responsible retail practices. Jon is actively involved in shaping the future of the low-dose THC market, working with brands, policymakers, and industry partners to support safe, regulated growth. He’s especially interested in what happens when the worlds of alcohol, cannabis, and retail collide—and how retailers can make the experience fun, approachable, and responsible for customers.

presenters.name: Jordan Weller
presenters.bio: Jordan Weller is the Taproom Manager & Events Coordinator at 56 Brewing, with nearly 15 years of experience in the craft beverage industry. Holding a degree in Music and Entertainment Business, he combines industry knowledge with creative event planning to produce engaging, community-driven experiences. Passionate about crafting community, Jordan creates events that bring people together over great beer and shared moments.
presenters.presentationTitle: Your Taproom Is Already a Third Place — Act Like It

presenters.name: Julie O'Donnell
presenters.bio: Julie O'Donnell joined Intuition Brewing as a beertender in June of 2024 and was promoted to Taproom Manager in 2025. She leads guest experience, staff development and assists with daily operations, coaching teams to deliver warm, consistent service. Julie's focus on her hospitality approach and staff training turns first-time visitors into regulars.

presenters.name: Kabel Lefto
presenters.bio: Kabel is the current Vice President of the MNCBG Board, after having served as an officer for a few years. Kabel has worked in breweries throughout the Twin Cities, and is currently the Packaging Technician at Insight Brewing Company.
presenters.presentationTitle: The Guild’s Role in Today’s Industry: A Discussion on What You Need Now

presenters.name: Liz Heimer
presenters.bio: As the co-owner navigating the many challenges of opening a newer brewery in the current craft beer landscape (Intuition Brewing), Liz is passionate about crafting unique and innovative ideas at the brewery. With a focus on creativity, Liz strives to push the boundaries to improve the customer experience in the taproom.

presenters.name: Marty Scott
presenters.bio: Marty Scott has been brewing commercially for more than 15 years. He is Revolution Brewing's Barrel Program Manager and is the Proprietor of Barrelponix.
presenters.presentationTitle: Stave New World: Methodologies for Managing the Modern (British) Brewer's Wood Cellar

presenters.name: Meghan Walsh
presenters.bio: As overdose prevention director, Meghan hosts regular naloxone trainings for community and professional groups and manages supply and kit distribution. While the Brewers Conference is an audience Meghan has not worked with before, she is delighted to be here and excited to share about the importance of naloxone as a tool for public health and safety.

presenters.name: Michaelann Gillis
presenters.bio: Michaelann Gillis has a degree in Hospitality Management and over 30 years working in restaurants, starting with her family owned taverns in Wisconsin. Michaelann is well equipped to hire and train front of house teams, however, writing beverage programs is her real passion. She has worked for several prominent breweries and restaurants around the Twin Cities in her career. She is now one of the Twin Cities most respected Bar & Beverage Consultants helping create and re-create successful bar programs around the Twin Cities.
presenters.presentationTitle: Restaurant Hospitality for Breweries - Turning your Brewery into a Successful F&B Operation

presenters.name: Nate Schneider
presenters.bio: Nate Schneider is the current President of the MNCBG Board of Directors, after serving two years and holding the positions of ICO and Treasurer. Nate has been in the industry 10 years in every aspect of the brewing industry, including sales, management, production, VP, and co-owner. Nathan served eight years in the Army National Guard.
presenters.presentationTitle: The Guild’s Role in Today’s Industry: A Discussion on What You Need Now

presenters.name: Robert Fulton
presenters.bio: Robert Fulton has worked in the hospitality industry since 1998, holding roles from busser to general manager. With experience spanning fine dining to multi-location operations, he’s led teams, created beverage programs, taught culinary classes, and consulted across the industry. For over 15 years, he has partnered with the MLBA, training countless businesses—from local restaurants to regional venues—on responsible alcohol sales and service. Now, Robert focuses on sales training, hospitality leadership, and empowering teams to serve legally, ethically, and confidently.
presenters.presentationTitle: S.A.L.E.S. Training: Selling Alcohol Legally, Effectively & Safely

presenters.name: Ryan Bandy
presenters.bio: Ryan Bandy is Chief Business Officer of Indeed Brewing Company, a Minneapolis- and Milwaukee-based brewery founded in 2012. Ryan joined Indeed over a decade ago, getting his start in packaging, snapping PakTechs onto cans and waxing tops of bottles. He’s since served as Sales Director, leading the brewery’s distribution and sales efforts, as well as Director of Experience, growing the community impact of Indeed’s events and creating welcoming taproom spaces for the brewery’s taprooms in Minneapolis and Milwaukee. With experience in every department of the brewery, from back of the house to the taproom, Ryan is uniquely aware of the ways brewery’s decision-making processes impact efficiencies at all levels of production, sales, and service.

presenters.name: Ryan Mayfield
presenters.bio: Ryan Mayfield is a leadership coach who helps brewery professionals build healthy leaders, strong teams, and thriving cultures. Through Craft Leadership, he equips clients with practical tools to lead with confidence, improve communication, and reduce daily frustrations. Craft has supported top breweries like Other Half, Rhinegeist, and Creature Comforts in navigating leadership and team challenges. Based in Tulsa, Ryan lives with his wife, teenage son, and opinionated beagle, Rooster.
presenters.presentationTitle: From Brewer to Boss: Equipping First-Time Leaders in the Brewery

presenters.name: Sara Phelps
presenters.bio: Sara graduated from the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities, earning a degree in Journalism and Political Science. Sara’s professional career began at a National Market Research firm where she served as a Senior Operations Manager and implemented and designed measurement tools for customer service for Coca Cola, Harrah’s Entertainment and General Motors. Her love of hospitality and restaurant operations brought her back to the industry in 2010 where she served as the Assistant General Manager of Smack Shack in Minneapolis, to turn the once famous food truck into one of Minneapolis’ most popular brick and mortar restaurants. Her strong attention to detail and commanding leadership style led to her role as Project Manager for The Lexington Restaurant Group where she was charged with completion of a long awaited 3 year renovation project. After achieving a restaurant opening, Sara moved to the role of General Manager and then Events Director for the property and served there until 2021. Sara’s commitment to exceptional guest service and her love of hospitality have led her to create her consultancy as skphelps Consulting LLC. Her work at Mise en Place allows her to share her love of front of house operations with clients at all levels of dining. She serves as an industry expert on Human Resources, FOH Training, Organizational Leadership, FOH Systems, & Staff Development."
presenters.presentationTitle: Restaurant Hospitality for Breweries - Turning your Brewery into a Successful F&B Operation

presenters.name: Stephanie Grant
presenters.bio: Stephanie Grant is an Atlanta-based content strategist and James Beard–nominated writer who helps breweries stand out online through storytelling. She has worked in the beer industry since 2017—starting as a writer covering beer and makers, then moving in-house as a brewery marketing coordinator. That combination of journalism and hands-on brewery experience shapes how she approaches storytelling today. Stephanie’s writing has appeared in CraftBeer.com, Good Beer Hunting, and The New Brewer. She now works independently with breweries to translate behind-the-scenes work into story-driven content that builds trust, reflects the in-person experience, and gives people a reason to choose them."
presenters.presentationTitle: Telling Your Brand Story Online: How to Connect and Stand Out Online

presenters.name: Steven Brown
presenters.bio: Steven Brown is the Founder and CEO of Nothing But Hemp, an award-winning cannabinoid product development and manufacturing company, and the Midwest Botanical Coalition. He launched one of the first hemp retail stores in the United States, which has grown into a national operation with products sold in liquor stores, hemp stores, dispensaries, and health shops nationwide. Under Brown’s leadership, the Minnesota-based manufacturing team produces over one million gummies per month, sonicates nano emulsion including hemp-derived THC products, mushroom supplements, and functional wellness formulations. Nothing But Hemp has received significant industry recognition, including Minnesota Monthly’s “Best Hemp Company” award and Feedspot’s recognition as one of the Top Hemp Blogs in the World. Products developed by Brown’s companies have also won a GreenState Award for Best Gummies, outperforming major brands such as Wana and Wyld. Beyond business, Brown has played an active role in cannabis policy, advocating at both the Minnesota State Capitol and in Washington, D.C., Steven helped shape Minnesota’s low-dose THC market and expanding opportunities for hemp businesses. Brown has been featured in major media outlets including High Times, Fox, CBS, and WCCO."
